[page[title]]

Treat business email as a managed platform capability with provider choice, queueing and operational visibility.

All platform domainsView the GitHub repositoryRead the documentation

What it owns

  • Mail-server configuration and named sender/receiver providers.
  • Queued and sent email records plus mailbox inspection.
  • SMTP, POP3 and Microsoft Graph support with a hosted sender loop.

Why the boundary matters

Applications request communication; the mail domain owns delivery mechanics, retryable queues and provider integration.

How it fits

The domain is published and tested independently, then composed through cCoder.Core when an application needs the complete platform. That keeps ownership visible while preserving a straightforward application bootstrap.

Getting started

The source, current README, sample hosts and tests live in cCoder.Mail on GitHub. The repository README is the version-specific starting point; the outline below explains how the pieces fit together.

Reference the package

<PackageReference Include="cCoder.Mail" Version="YOUR_VERSION" />

During coordinated local development the repositories may substitute a sibling ProjectReference. Published applications should normally consume the agreed package version so the dependency boundary remains explicit.

Register it in the host

builder.Services.AddMailWeb(/* provider and platform configuration */);
app.StartMailWeb();

// Sender/receiver workers use AddMailHostedServices and StartMailHostedServices.

Configure and run it

Create MailServer records and register named SMTP, POP3 or Microsoft Graph sender/receiver providers. Keep credentials in deployment configuration or secret storage rather than page or workflow definitions.

Consume the capability

Applications enqueue QueuedEmail records; the hosted sender owns delivery and produces SentEmail history. Consumers should request communication and observe status instead of calling a provider SDK from each business domain.

Build and verify from source

git clone https://github.com/ccoder-co-uk/cCoder.Mail.git
cd cCoder.Mail
dotnet build
dotnet test

Use the repository-specific solution and test commands from its README when working on the domain itself; the standalone and acceptance-test hosts show the supported application boundary more accurately than an isolated snippet can.
